standard_prerequisites.name: A map of sheaves of sets is an isomorphism if and only if it is an isomorphism on all stalks (lemma-points-exactness)

core_obligations: The functoriality of the sheafification construction applied to phi: F -> G yields the commutative square F -> F# -> Pi(F) over G -> G# -> Pi(G) (proof lines 1814-1823). The square shows the composite F -> F# -> G# -> Pi(G) agrees with F -> G -> G# -> Pi(G). It suffices to show the canonical map G -> G# is an isomorphism (proof line 1824). By the stalkwise criterion for isomorphisms of sheaves of sets (proof lines 1824-1827), this holds once G_x -> G#_x is bijective for every x; and this is exactly the equality of stalks under sheafification (proof lines 1827-1830). Hence phi: F -> G factors uniquely through F -> F#, uniqueness following because F -> F# has sheafification image generating all stalks of F# (proof lines 1813-1830).
proof_roadmap: Build the functorial commutative square and reduce to G = G# (proof lines 1814-1824).
Check stalkwise bijectivity via the points-exactness criterion and the stalk equality (proof lines 1824-1830).
